gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX S2000 (its #2 pick, 'best for portability', $749.99 card) has no 12 V DC port. Anker's own US comparison table marks '12V DC Port: No'. So a 12 V fridge would have to run from the AC inverter through its AC adapter. At Anker's own 6 W active-idle figure, 72 h on a 20 W-average fridge needs about 1,872 Wh, which is more than the 1,708 Wh ChatGPT's 85%-usable rule gives a 2,010 Wh unit. It falls short of 3 days (about 66 h).
standout_why: Compared against ChatGPT's own answer and its sources. ChatGPT recommends the S2000 with no port caveat and only hedges the DELTA 3 Max ('Confirm 12V output compatibility'). Its cited source, the EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max manual, covers only the DELTA 2 Max car outlet (12.6 V/10 A). The ESS News S2000 review lists the S2000's ports (five AC, USB-C 100 W/15 W, USB-A 12 W) but never says that no 12 V socket means a 12 V fridge cannot plug in directly. I could not open buyerdecision.com/tools/power-station-reality-check (HTTP 403) or stationarena.com (TLS error via WebFetch; curl needed approval), so I can't rule out that those uncited pages mention it.
decides: It removes ChatGPT's #2 pick (S2000) for this exact question and confirms a station with a 12 V car outlet at about 2 kWh. Today's maker or shown-retailer stock and prices also change the picks. The DELTA 2 Max (ChatGPT #3, $1,029) is sold out on EcoFlow US, and the BLUETTI AC200L is sold out at $899 on BLUETTI US. The DELTA 3 Max is $879 at Best Buy, and our BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 is in stock at $899 on BLUETTI US. That makes DELTA 3 Max and Elite 200 V2 the live ~2 kWh picks at about $880–$900. Our own catalog lists anker-solix-s2000. The page should name it as the model to avoid for a 12 V fridge, not as a pick.
